newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania floods hit more towns and villages.
newsitem.headline: Romania floods hit more towns and villages.

text.p: Rivers swollen by days of rain inundated more Romanian towns and villages on Tuesday, hitting the region of the River Danube delta near the border with Ukraine particularly badly.
The environment ministry said seven rivers were at flood stage throughout the country, down from 17 on Monday.

But over 1,000 hectares of farmland remained under water and 1,030 families had been forced from their homes -- three times more than the previous day. One person died at the weekend near the border with ex-Soviet Moldova.

The worst damage was recorded in Tulcea region, where high water near the Danube sent 200 families from their homes, knocked out water supplies and shut down a hospital. The Danube was on the rise, but still well below flood levels.
In the steel-producing town of Resita, near the border with Serbia, 300 houses were evacuated and officials brought in drinking water supplies by tanker truck.
A top agricultural official on Monday said harvesting of what officials say is a bumper wheat crop would be seriously delayed by the floods. But they provided no figures for estimated crop losses.
Weather forecasters said conditions would improve in the next 24 hours, with only occasional showers in mountain areas.
Flooding last month killed 12 people in the region of Bihor, near the Hungarian border.
